text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI

- Prime Minister Majali says always ready for dialogue with Moslem Brotherhood if they want it. Brotherhood leader says government has shut door to dialogue. First opposition party declares it is boycotting elections.
- Majali says peace a strategic option, not a tactic. Jordan's ties with Arab states are at best possible level.
- Customs chief says Jordan will implement unified customs system from start of next year.
- Foreign buying orders on Amman stock exchange reached 44.2 million ($62 million) in first half of this year, bourse says.
AD-DUSTOUR
- Majali says no plans to extend parliament beyond November or to revoke Moslem Brotherhood's permit.
- Unions and three political parties say they will boycott parliamentary elections.
- Former Prime Minister Kabariti appointed head of Jordan Kuwait Bank.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Moslem Brotherhood head Abdul-Majid al-Thuneibat says government has closed door to dialogue, warns against any government pressure on movement.
AL-ASWAQ
- Royal decree expected within two days dissolving parliament in preparation for elections.
- Palestinians renew invitation for Majali to visit Gaza.
- Foreign Minister Tarawnah says Jordan will take part in Qatar's Middle East economic summit.

- Cabinet approves strategy for restructuring loss-making Royal Jordanian airlines ahead of privatisation. Plan calls for airline to be registered as company owned by Royal Jordanian and a strategic partner, and get it operating on commercial basis.
JORDAN TIMES
- Government says elections on time, ready for dialogue.
- Majali to visit Gaza Strip in bid to unlock Palestinian-Israeli talks.
